# How a Bicycle Gear System Works

A bicycle gear system transfers your pedaling power to the wheels while allowing you to choose different speed-to-effort ratios. The core components are the chainrings (front gears), the cassette (rear gears), and the chain that connects them.

**The basics:** Your feet push down on the pedals, which rotate the crank arm and the chainring attached to it. The chain, a loop of metal links, wraps around the chainring and pulls the rear cog (one of the gears on the cassette) forward. As the rear cog turns, it rotates your rear wheel, propelling the bicycle forward.
